subject: Inference metrics sprint: cache sensitivity + per-1M token probe
messages:
From: Elena Rojas <elena@mistytech.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: workload + questions on cache/batching economics

Thanks again for the demo this morning — good clarity on the routing and rollback behavior. As promised, attaching a small slice of the production workload (sample_workload.json) and a recent API trace (cache_trace_misty.csv).

A few prioritized asks to help us compare vendors and prepare our procurement brief: 
- Can you run a per-1M-token cost estimate for our workload across: Redwood-hosted, Hyperscaler-A managed endpoints (our rough numbers attached from their pricing sheet), and an on-prem quantized run?
- We care about latency at 95th and 99th pct — can you show expected P95/P99 at 8- and 64-token batching windows?
- Cache hit sensitivity: show unit-econ delta for cache hit rates: 40%, 70%, 95%.

Constraints: our security team will only accept evidence of prefix caching behavior and an SLO for cache key traceability. Also include any assumptions about tokenization differences that materially affect per-1M numbers.

Next step: a short follow-up call next week to review test plan and timelines. 

Thanks,
Elena
Sr. ML Platform Lead
MistyTech Solutions
[Attachment: sample_workload.json (json)]
[Attachment: cache_trace_misty.csv (csv)]

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
To: Elena Rojas <elena@mistytech.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: workload + questions on cache/batching economics

Elena — great notes and helpful trace, thanks. High-level recap and our proposed test matrix below.

Quick summary (so you can paste into procurement): 
- Per-1M token baseline (approx, raw estimates): Redwood-hosted (unquantized, default batching): $18 per 1M tokens; Hyperscaler-A managed (public price + estimated infra cost): $34 per 1M; On-prem quantized (INT8 path): $6–$9 per 1M depending on util. 
  - These are illustrative; final numbers will come from the actual probe run against your sample_workload.json.

Proposed probe matrix (what we'll run this week):
1) Baseline throughput runs (no KV/prefix caching) — measure P95/P99 and cost per 1M tokens at 8-token and 64-token batch windows.
2) Cache sensitivity sweep — run the workload with programmatic cache stubs to force hit rates at 40%, 70%, 95% and measure token-level cost delta (we'll capture cache hit ratio at request level).
3) Quantization delta — 16-bit float vs INT8 path on a dedicated machine to surface quality vs cost tradeoff.
4) Cross-compare Hyperscaler-A: we will run the same sample_workload against their managed endpoint (you gave us access token) to collect P95/P99 and token counts.

Deliverables and timeline: 
- Raw probe results + per-1M token CSVs (one per test) — 3 business days.
- One-page executive summary with clear unit-econ lines for procurement — 5 business days.
- SLO/caching evidence doc (how cache keys are traced, expiry behavior) — included in the executive summary.

Assumptions and caveats: 
- Tokenization differences: small delta expected (±2–6%) depending on tokenizer; we'll normalize to MistyTech's counts in the spreadsheet.
- We assume the Hyperscaler-A endpoint you provided is representative of their lowest-latency tier; if it's behind a gateway that batches at 200ms, that will inflate P95.

Action items: 
- Elena: confirm access token for Hyperscaler-A and any IP allowlists we need to hit their endpoint.
- Ben: allocate a dedicated pod for INT8 quant runs and reserve time Friday AM.
- Vanessa: I'll share the probe command lines and a small runbook for your security team to validate cache tracing.

If that sounds good I'll kick off the baseline today and post preliminary numbers by Friday. I'm copying Ben and Vanessa for ops support.

— Jasmine
Business Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_unit_econ_estimate.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Cc: Elena Rojas <elena@mistytech.com>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2026 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: workload + questions on cache/batching economics

Sounds good — I've reserved a dedicated slot on our dedicated pool for Friday 08:00–11:00 PT for the INT8 runs. I'll also spin up a small job to replay cache_trace_misty.csv to validate hit-rate instrumentation.

One operational note: for the high-hit-rate (95%) run we'll need a warm KV cache; Jasmine, can you confirm the runbook includes a warmup pass and the number of unique keys to emulate?

Ben
Sr. Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks team — that timeline works for us. Quick answers: 
- Hyperscaler-A token is live and I've sent a separate secure note to your ops alias with the token and host.
- Warmup: for the 95% cache run, emulate 25k unique keys and a 30-minute warm window.
- Procurement ask: can you provide a short SOW and an estimate line item for the probe (roughly < $5k preferrable)? If you can include optional line items for on-prem quant and extended retention of logs, that would help.

I'll schedule a 30-minute follow-up next Tuesday to review the initial CSVs and the executive one-pager.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Elena
